abstract: This IMF paper examines AI's impact on global employment and skill requirements. The research finds that approximately 40% of global employment is exposed to AI, rising to 60% in advanced economies, with 10% of jobs in advanced economies already requiring at least one new skill. The study addresses the critical challenge of bridging skill gaps to ensure workers can adapt to the AI-driven labor market transformation.
keyFindings: Around 40% of global employment is exposed to AI, compared to 60% in advanced economies.
10% of jobs in advanced economies currently require at least one new skill due to AI integration.
Skill gap bridging is essential for workforce adaptation in the AI age.
Advanced economies face more pronounced AI-driven labor market disruption than developing economies.
